mbm-0118.clue: I can make one egg stand still.
mbm-0118.quote: I balance a wooden egg on the back of my hand while telling a terrible joke. The trick is easy. The hard part is keeping my hand steady when Dad laughs a line early.

mbm-0119.clue: Those faded whiskers once dried dishes.
mbm-0119.quote: My aunt’s old dish towel had a cat on it with hardly any face left. I stitched it into her lap quilt and gave it blue whiskers. She recognized it by the crooked tail.

mbm-0120.clue: I know when the best seat is empty.
mbm-0120.quote: The cinema’s back row has a spring that hums during the opening music. When I go with my brother, I put my coat on that seat and we get a tiny orchestra between us.

mbm-0121.clue: My needle case has a boarding pass inside.
mbm-0121.quote: I sewed a loose button onto a stranger’s coat while we waited for the train. She drew me a little bird on the reverse of her ticket. It’s the lid of my sewing tin now.

mbm-0122.clue: There’s a lighthouse in my headphones.
mbm-0122.quote: My radio friend sends one slow greeting whenever he starts the night shift at the lighthouse. I put a paper boat beside the receiver and move it an inch each time I hear from him.

mbm-0123.clue: That white strip comes out at night.
mbm-0123.quote: I sewed a band of pale ribbon along the edge of a dark quilt. In moonlight it looks like a road. My nephew drives his wooden bus along it after lights out.

mbm-0124.clue: There’s a sunflower in my pencil bag.
mbm-0124.quote: I was lining up my first proper putt when a seed dropped out of my pocket. A sunflower came up behind the green that summer. I count it as the best thing I planted there.

mbm-0125.clue: We walk to the second echo.
mbm-0125.quote: I call hello from a bend in our trail. The first answer is a cliff. The second is Mum round the next bend, calling me to hurry up with the cocoa.

mbm-0126.quote: A crack ran the whole length of a flowerpot I was decorating. I turned it into the stem of a poppy and painted the bloom right where the chip was. The plant inside is still jealous.

mbm-0127.clue: I only meant to paint one pear.
mbm-0127.quote: I used the same pear for a week of still lifes. Its green shoulder turned gold, then brown, and on Friday I baked the whole series into a tart.

mbm-0128.clue: I am banned from naming the towns.
mbm-0128.quote: We build the board out of cardboard squares. My town kept landing on the tablecloth seam, so I named it Wrinkle Junction. Now every railway has to go through there.

mbm-0129.clue: There’s a tiny ladder in my belt.
mbm-0129.quote: I stamped a row of ladder rungs inside the belt I made for my first job. Every time I learned something new, I darkened another rung with wax. There’s room for plenty more.

mbm-0130.clue: My loudest move is my smallest.
mbm-0130.quote: At our kitchen domino table, my grandma lays the last tile down so softly we lean right in. Then she taps the table with her teaspoon. That little tink means she’s won.

mbm-0131.clue: You get an extra stroke if you ring the bell.
mbm-0131.quote: The owner of our mini-golf place hung a bicycle bell in the windmill doorway. I’ve never won on points. I have absolutely won on noise.

mbm-0132.clue: The net is where the shadows meet.
mbm-0132.quote: Our beach court is between two palms. At about five the shadows touch right under the net. That’s when we switch ends and give the shorter player the shade.

mbm-0133.clue: My newest scarf has a staircase in it.
mbm-0133.quote: I missed a stitch on the train every time the doors opened. When I unrolled the scarf I could see all eight stops. I put a tassel on the one where my sister lives.

mbm-0134.clue: Our best microphone is a soup spoon.
mbm-0134.quote: When our bassist’s kid comes to practice, we set a wooden spoon upside down in a mug. She sings the count-in into it. Nobody starts till she’s ready.

mbm-0135.clue: Watch what happens when we pause the tape.
mbm-0135.quote: We copied the running poses from our favorite cartoon onto scraps of paper. When you flip the stack the hero runs straight out of his shoes. My page is the flying left boot.

mbm-0136.clue: I call it the underwater deck.
mbm-0136.quote: My card sleeves fogged up on the way to a tournament. Every monster looked like it lived at the bottom of the sea. I still play the kelp witch first, in case the weather helps.

mbm-0137.clue: I can hear our washing line.
mbm-0137.quote: When the wind swings the antenna against the clothespin on the line, I get three little clicks in my headphones. That’s how I know the laundry will be dry before my radio chat ends.

mbm-0138.clue: My best trail marker is a hot pink mitten.
mbm-0138.quote: I lost one on the ridge last winter. In spring somebody had put it on a post, pointing toward the summit. I took a different way back so I could follow its directions.

mbm-0139.clue: Open this one against the sky.
mbm-0139.quote: I folded the paper twice too many times cutting a row of little houses. When I opened it, I had a whole pink neighborhood. We strung it between our balconies for supper.

mbm-0140.clue: The blurry one is my favorite.
mbm-0140.quote: I tried a slow shutter at my grandfather’s birthday. Everyone is still except his waving hand. In the print it looks as if he has been waving hello for a whole minute.

mbm-0141.quote: On my first jump I expected the wind to keep roaring. Then the canopy opened, my ears went quiet, and I heard a cow in the field below. I laughed all the way down.

mbm-0142.clue: I wax the short skis first.
mbm-0142.quote: My little cousin watches me tune our skis. I finish hers before mine so she can test the slide on the last patch of snow by the shed. Her review is always one long whee.
